archetype.name: Gunslinger (vertical, turnover-prone)
archetype.definition: A pocket thrower who wins by pushing the ball downfield and into tight windows, and has always paid for that aggression with interceptions, which he does again this year with less accuracy than his last two seasons.

report.headline: Deep shots still land; the short game and turnovers are sinking him.
report.take:
Darnold is back as Seattle's QB1 after a murky first half. The dossier credits Drew Lock with the Week 2-6 starts, yet Darnold logged full snaps in Weeks 3 through 6. Lock is now inactive, so this is Darnold's offense again. What he has been is a split personality. On throws of 10+ air yards he has been very good: +0.453 EPA per attempt and a +3.6 CPOE, and on the 20 deep attempts the deep ball has been his best play. On everything under 10 yards he has been a liability, at -0.177 EPA per attempt with a -5.5 CPOE. That short bucket outweighs the downfield gains, and it is why his passing EPA per dropback (-0.072) sits 33rd of 47 even though his yards per attempt is dead on the league average.

The drop from 2025 is real and steep. Completion rate is down 7.5 points, YPA is down nearly a point and a half, and CPOE has fallen from +5.2 to roughly -2. The cause doesn't look like raw ball placement. His charted bad-throw rate of 9.5% ranks 2nd of 38, better than last year's 13.6%. What changed is the environment and the decisions. He is pressured on 26.7% of dropbacks (35th of 38). The run game ranks 29th in EPA. The offense passes well below expectation, which leaves him in long third downs: the average is 8.3 to go, he converts 30.6%, and third-down EPA is -0.301. His aggressiveness is also up 5.5 points from last year, which fits an interception rate of 4.3%, 41st of 47.

The numbers also hide how much of the passing game runs through one player. Jaxon Smith-Njigba has 68 targets at +0.585 EPA each, adding up to +39.8. Throws to AJ Barner (-15.2) and Rashid Shaheed (-10.4) have handed most of that back. Behind-the-line throws alone have cost -18.9 EPA. When Darnold is not throwing to JSN or over the top, the offense is mostly losing ground.

The career record frames all of this. Interceptions have been part of him in every full season, with his 2025 total ranking 61st of 63 even in a 14-3 year. The accuracy he showed in 2024-25, though, was a real level he reached, not a fluke. The likeliest path is a partial rebound in efficiency when protection holds, as it did against Kansas City. The turnover rate will stay costly.

strengths.title: Downfield accuracy and big-play throws
strengths.body: His 20+ yard attempts have produced +1.114 EPA each with a +15.3 CPOE, and the whole 10+ group is strongly positive. Twenty deep attempts is a hint, not a fact, and that CPOE will cool. Still, his 2024-25 seasons showed the same willingness and touch on intermediate and deep throws. The intermediate bucket's 57.4% success rate is the steadier sign that this skill is real.

strengths.title: Ball placement is not the problem
strengths.body: His charted bad-throw rate ranks 2nd of 38, an improvement on last year. Next Gen's tracking CPOE is also slightly positive at +0.77, even though the play-by-play CPOE is negative. That points to the low completion rate coming from situation, pressure and target quality rather than a broken throwing motion, which makes a rebound more plausible.

strengths.title: Feeding Smith-Njigba pays
strengths.body: JSN has been targeted 68 times at +0.585 EPA per target, carrying the passing game almost by himself. Target volume and efficiency this concentrated in one receiver usually hold. As long as JSN is on the field, Darnold has a reliable way to move the ball.

concerns.title: Interceptions, as always
concerns.body: A 4.3% interception rate ranks 41st of 47, and the 22-interception pace would be the worst of his career. It isn't new: he ranked 48th or worse in interceptions in nearly every full season, including 2025. Higher aggressiveness this year feeds it. Expect some regression from the current rate, but he will stay below average here.

concerns.title: Short game is a dead zone
concerns.body: Under-10 throws are at -0.177 EPA, and behind-the-line throws have cost -18.9 EPA on 45 attempts. Screens and checkdowns get blown up when the run game ranks 29th and the offense's hit rate ranks 29th. Throws to Barner and Shaheed have been net-negative too. Part of this is the offense around him, but a -6.1 CPOE on short throws is on him as well.

concerns.title: Pressure and long third downs
concerns.body: He is pressured on 26.7% of dropbacks, 35th of 38, and his third downs average 8.3 yards to go, where he has posted -0.301 EPA. Close games have been his worst setting, at -0.229 EPA when within one score. Left tackle Charles Cross missed Week 8, and that game produced a -16.9 CPOE. Better health up front is what would most likely change this.

trend.note: His best game came in Week 7 against Kansas City: +12.2 EPA while pressured on only 6.7% of dropbacks. A week later Chicago held him to a -16.9 CPOE with Cross out. His last three games show better EPA per dropback than his season (-0.009) but worse accuracy (-5.8 CPOE), so the line swings with protection.

nextGame.headline: A bottom-tier pass defense, but a lopsided script may cap volume
nextGame.body:
Arizona's defense is ranked 31st against the pass by EPA. It ranks 30th in explosive passes allowed, 24th on deep throws and 29th on short throws. It allows 2.63 passing touchdowns a game to quarterbacks, 31st in the league. That fits Darnold well: his downfield throws should find room, and even his weak short game faces a soft underneath defense. The catch is its 8th-ranked sack rate. A quarterback pressured as often as Darnold, with an interception habit, can still give away possessions. Arizona's run defense is 7th, which may push Seattle to throw more than usual early.

On availability, Cross (98% of snaps) and Shaheed were inactive in Week 8, and both carry a Nov. 8 return estimate. Cross's return matters far more for Darnold's pressure numbers; treat both as uncertain until game day. Arizona is without DT Walter Nolen III, which thins its interior rush. Its offense is banged up too: WR Michael Wilson has broken ribs, Kendrick Bourne is out for the season, and RBs Jeremiyah Love and Bam Knight are questionable. As 11.5-point favorites with a strong defense, Seattle could build a lead and lean on the run in the second half. That would cut Darnold's attempts even if his efficiency is good.

keyMatchups.title: JSN against a soft WR1 defense
keyMatchups.body: Arizona has allowed +0.67 EPA per target to opposing WR1s, 30th in the league. Smith-Njigba is already Darnold's most efficient read by a wide margin. This is the most likely source of his big plays and touchdowns.

keyMatchups.title: Arizona's pass rush vs. Seattle's line
keyMatchups.body: Arizona's sack rate ranks 8th, and Darnold's pressure rate ranks 35th of 38. Whether Cross plays decides whether this looks like the Kansas City game or the Chicago game.

keyMatchups.title: Blowout script
keyMatchups.body: With Seattle a heavy favorite, a big lead would mean run-heavy late downs. Darnold has been efficient on the few plays he's had while leading by 9 or more. Expect efficiency, but maybe not volume.

nextGame.watch: Whether Charles Cross is active at left tackle: Darnold's accuracy and sack numbers have tracked his protection all year.

restOfSeason.body:
Darnold is more likely to settle somewhere between this season and his 2024-25 form than to stay at a -0.072 EPA per dropback. His ball placement charts well, his downfield game works, and his offense has one dependable target. The current negative CPOE looks more like situation and protection than a collapse in skill. What won't fully regress is the turnover rate. He has thrown interceptions in volume in every season, and his rising aggressiveness keeps that risk high. The deep-ball efficiency will come down as the sample grows, so the big games will be fewer than the deep split suggests.

Volume is capped by a run-leaning offense, 27th in pass rate over expected, and by a top-five defense that will create leads. A fair expectation is roughly 215-260 passing yards a game with 1.2-1.9 touchdowns and about an interception a game. A healthy line and some reliable targets beyond JSN would push that toward the top of the range.
swingFactors: Charles Cross's health and pass protection
Whether a second target emerges beyond Smith-Njigba
Hold on the QB1 job given the Lock situation

confidence.note: Seven games of mixed starter and backup roles, a muddled start log and a small deep-ball sample; the interception trend is backed by his whole career.
